summary: Cross-project cloud IAM role mapping and access request for infra engineers
description:
Issue summary: Several infra engineers need temporary cross-project access in both AWS and GCP to diagnose a networking/permission problem surfaced during a private cluster migration. Request: establish least-privilege, time-bound role mappings between the 'infra-ops' GCP project and the 'platform-prod' GCP project, and create an AWS IAM role assumption path from Redwood-staff accounts to the production account for specific SRE personas.

Impact: Engineers are blocked from collecting instance-level logs, describing certain VPC connectors, and running diagnostic jobs in the target projects. This is delaying a staged migration and causing elevated alerting noise as automated runbooks retry and fail.

Environment: Production (prod) across multi-cloud: GCP (europe-west1 primary), AWS (us-east-1, us-west-2).

Request details: 1) Define and apply GCP IAM custom role(s) that allow iam.serviceAccounts.get, compute.instances.get, compute.networks.list limited to resources in the target projects. 2) Configure IAM bindings so members in the 'redwood-infra-eng' Google Group can impersonate a service account in the target project using iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy/allow impersonation. 3) In AWS, create a cross-account role (AssumeRole) named RedwoodInfraDiagnosticRole in the production account with a trust policy for the Redwood-staff AWS account IDs (list provided privately) and scoped policies that allow ec2:DescribeInstances, logs:GetLogEvents, logs:DescribeLogGroups, and sts:AssumeRole chaining only to a short-lived diagnostics role. 4) All changes must be time-bound (72 hours) by default and logged to audit (Cloud Audit Logs/CloudTrail) with tags 'temp_access_migration'.

Acceptance criteria: - Infra engineers in the specified groups can perform listed diagnostics for up to 72 hours. - All actions are covered by audit logs with a retention label. - There is a documented rollback that revokes access at expiry or on-demand.

Notes: Customer-facing incidents are not involved; this is internal to migration workstreams.
steps_to_reproduce: Not an application bug. Repro steps for blocked behavior: 1) Attempt to list network connectors in target GCP project using gcloud compute networks list --project=platform-prod -> Permission denied. 2) Attempt to get logs from a production EC2 instance via aws logs get-log-events -> AccessDenied. 3) Attempt to impersonate target service account -> iam.serviceAccounts.getIamPolicy returns 403. These steps can be reproduced by an engineer without elevated membership in the target projects.
logs:
GCP denied response samples: 
- "Error: Permission 'compute.networks.list' denied on resource project 'platform-prod'" (2026-03-12T16:03:21Z).
AWS denied response sample: 
- "An error occurred (AccessDenied) when calling the DescribeInstances operation: User is not authorized to perform: ec2:DescribeInstances" (2026-03-12T16:12:04Z).
investigation_notes:
2026-03-13: Triage by Priya. Confirmed issue is permissions surface, not networking. Verified group memberships for two engineers: membership shows in Google Groups but no IAM bindings in target project. Checked Cloud Audit Logs: no prior role binding events for 'redwood-infra-eng' group.

Hypotheses: 1) Role mappings were not propagated when the platform-prod project was created under a different org folder. 2) Pending org policy prevents cross-project service account impersonation. 3) In AWS, SCPs or account-level deny rules block AssumeRole from staff accounts.

Evidence gathered: - GCP Organization policies show 'restrictServiceAccountDelegation' enabled at org level (affects impersonation). - AWS SCP audit shows a Deny for 'sts:AssumeRole' from external principal for one prod account (account 987654321098).

Next steps: 1) SRE/Cloud Infra to propose exact custom role definitions. 2) Security to review org policy exception request for impersonation (if required). 3) Create ephemeral roles and apply tagging. Assigned to Marco to coordinate with Security and Cloud Infra.
action_items: Draft GCP custom role YAML and test in staging
Open security exception ticket for org policy change if needed
Create AWS cross-account AssumeRole with time-bound sessionDuration
Add audit tags and update runbook with revocation steps
resolution: In progress: Preliminary GCP custom role draft created and reviewed with Cloud Infra. Security requested more context for org policy exception; submitted SEC-EXC-77 with justification and TTL. AWS role created in a sandbox account for testing; production role blocked by SCP — security will coordinate with finance-owned account to authorize temporary trust. Final revocation automation will be implemented using an expiry Lambda that removes the binding at 72 hours and emits a Jira comment. No permanent privileges granted.
follow_up: After access is granted and migration tasks complete, runbook update required: add a section 'temporary cross-project access for migrations' with step-by-step template, CLI snippets, and automated revocation playbook. Also schedule a post-mortem to evaluate why initial project onboarding missed these role mappings.
